input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The join separator logic was inverted during the refactor. The original code used "; " when any_prefix_is_slash was true and " / " otherwise. The new code uses "; " when it is false and " / " when it is true.
- rationale: Trigger: any option with both primary and secondary opts, such as a boolean flag like --shout/--no-shout. Originally the non-slash case was joined with " / " ('--shout / --no-shout'). Now it is joined with "; " ('--shout; --no-shout'). Impact: help output changes for every boolean flag, and for slash-prefix options such as /debug;/no-debug the separator is also flipped.
critique: The finding pinpoints the inverted any_prefix_is_slash condition in separator selection and gives the same failure: --shout/--no-shout renders as '--shout; --no-shout', and slash-prefixed options get ' / '. This is the same mechanism and outcome as the labeled defect.
